question: By what architectural pathway can tokens beyond the 1,024-token sliding window still affect routing in Gemma4 26B-A4B, and what empirical condition in experiment V4 determines whether long sessions remain mandatory or shorter L ≥ 2,048 sessions are permitted?

evidence.heading: 3.1 Why v1's snippets could not represent production routing
evidence.quote: **25 of the 30 layers use sliding-window attention with `n_swa = 1 024`** (`gemma4.attention.sliding_window = 1024`, pattern `[T,T,T,T,T,F,…]`); only the 5 global layers (5, 11, 17, 23, 29) attend beyond 1 024 tokens. Deep-context influence on routing therefore flows through those five layers' residual contributions to all subsequent layers.

evidence.heading: 6.4 V3 — Determinism, ubatch invariance, chunk independence, depth (≈ 45 min)
evidence.quote: **Depth matters** if `JSD_deep > JSD_between-spans` in ≥ 15/30 layers ⇒ long sessions stay mandatory. Otherwise ⇒ record "no first-order depth effect at 8 k", allow `L ≥ 2 048` sessions for cost

key_facts: residual contributions from the 5 global layers (5, 11, 17, 23, 29) beyond n_swa = 1 024
V4 criterion: JSD_deep > JSD_between-spans in ≥ 15/30 layers

question: How does Spec-Experts Phase 2 KV tiering differ from LocalAI's KV management, and what per-tier token counts across VRAM, RAM, and disk sum to its 18,432-token effective context?

evidence.heading: 2. Feature-by-Feature Comparison
evidence.quote: | P2 — KV tiering | llama-server RAM prompt cache (`--cache-ram`), KV quant (`-ctk/-ctv`); whole-model LRU eviction; no disk KV tier | VRAM→RAM→Disk `.kvbin` per-token tiering — **unique** |

evidence.heading: 3.3.1 Memory Hierarchy Design
evidence.quote: $$\text{ctx}_{\text{eff}} = N_{\text{VRAM}} + N_{\text{RAM}} + N_{\text{disk}} \approx 2{,}048 + 4{,}096 + 12{,}288 = 18{,}432 \text{ tokens}$$

key_facts: LocalAI uses --cache-ram, -ctk/-ctv KV quant, whole-model LRU, and no disk tier

question: In the Tier 2 per-token routing capture, which compute-graph tensor name is read, how is last-layer router pruning avoided, and how were struct offsets obtained for Windows b8679 without shipped headers?

evidence.heading: 4.3 Measurement Methods
evidence.quote: Python ctypes loads the llama.cpp shared libraries and, in the per-node callback of the compute graph, reads the tensor `ffn_moe_topk-L` (the router top-k indices of each layer). The struct field offsets are not hand-transcribed but measured by compiling a small program against the build's own headers (`config/tier2_layouts/`); to keep the router tensor of the last layer from being pruned to the output tokens, logits are requested for every token.

evidence.heading: 5.4 Per-token Temporal Locality (Tier 2)
evidence.quote: Windows b8679 ships no headers, so the struct offsets were inferred from the gx10 layout minus the fields added after b8679 (`config/tier2_layouts/b8679.json`) and validated by behaviour (the context is created and every layer yields exactly one row per token).

key_facts: request logits for every token to avoid last-layer pruning
b8679 offsets inferred from gx10 layout minus post-b8679 fields (config/tier2_layouts/b8679.json) and validated by behaviour
